judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Reading Skills (shared Grade R coordinate, rank 0): the first is Term 1 under sub-strand 'Begins to make meaning of written text' ('Recognises own name and names of at least five other children in the class'), the second is Term 2 under sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills' ('Uses pictures to ‘read’ simple phrase or caption books'). They are coherent, complementary emergent-reading meaning-making strategies within the same skill area, and the Term 1 to Term 2 order would permit a forward developmental claim, but the evidence shows two distinct routes into print — whole-word/name sight recognition versus picture-cued 'reading' of captions — with no textual indication that name recognition is the capability that supports success with caption books (no shared letters, words, or increasing text complexity chain). LC tags only share the generic 'emergent reading' token and LC text overlap is limited to stopwords, so the overlap evidence is weak and does not establish dependency. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment; note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which bounds this reading of the full source.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 4, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', printed in the same table (window 52) under different sub-strands: 'Group Guided Reading:' (first: 'Uses phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills and comprehension skills to make meaning') and 'Paired/Independent Reading' (second: 'Reads own and others' writing'). They are substantively coherent as complementary reading contexts in one term's reading programme — strategic decoding/comprehension work with the teacher, and paired/independent reading of self- and peer-produced texts — so this is meaningful instructional coherence rather than mere shared wording (lexical overlap is only 'and'/'ing' and the LC tag overlap is just 'reading'). It is not buildsTowards in either direction: the two bullets are delivered concurrently in the same Grade and Term, and the bounded evidence shows no pair-specific expansion (no longer or more complex texts, no added letter/phonic scope, no stated increase in independence relative to the other statement); the only link offered for direction is the generic claim that decoding underpins all reading, which would apply to every reading statement and does not meet the same-rank substantive-extension requirement. Direction is therefore null. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), the second endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, and the Grade/Term ancestors carry merge decisions and other upstream audit context that could not be independently resolved.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 1 Skills (coordinate rank 1, status resolved). The first sits under Grade 1 / Term 2 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities with the statement 'Listens to stories and identifies the main idea' (LCs 'Listens to stories' and 'Identifies the main idea of a story'; tags listening, oral, stories, comprehension, main idea). The second sits under Grade 1 / Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading with 'Recognises cause and effect in a story. The girl got into trouble because she broke a window' (LC tags cause and effect, comprehension, shared reading, story). They share genuine instructional coherence: both are narrative-comprehension skills applied to stories within the same grade, and competence in attending to and making sense of stories orally complements recognising causal relations in a shared-reading text. However, the evidence does not establish a developmental dependency: identifying a story's main idea and recognising cause and effect are distinct comprehension strategies in different skill areas and modalities, and the connecting signals are weak (one shared tag 'comprehension', jaccard 0.083; sfi token overlap limited to 'and'/'the'; trigram overlap 'sto'/'tor'). No evidence shows expanded capability of the same skill (more text, more independence, greater complexity of the same operation), so the permitted earlier-to-later-term buildsTowards is not substantiated and symmetric relatesTo is the correct complete judgment with null direction. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints carry truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, and every endpoint and ancestor carries upstream audit/merge context that must be inspected before interpreting its evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 2, Term 3, Reading and Phonics (resolved coordinate rank 2, same Term), but under different printed sub-strands: the second is a Phonics bullet ('Groups common words into sound families such as 'oy', 'oi'; 'ay', 'ai''), the first is a Group Guided Reading bullet ('Uses sight words, phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills when reading'). The phonics skill establishes explicit word-level grapheme/sound-pattern knowledge at the isolated-word level, which is one of the decoding resources the guided-reading statement requires learners to deploy flexibly alongside sight words, context and structure while reading connected text. Proficiency with sound families therefore plausibly supports success in applied, integrated decoding during reading, giving a same-Term lower-to-higher-complexity direction from the second to the first endpoint; the reverse (applied reading strategies supporting a narrower pattern-grouping task) is less supported. Shared ancestry, page 97 proximity and the single shared LC tag 'phonics' alone were not treated as sufficient; the substantive basis is the word-level-pattern to applied-decoding relationship in the statement texts. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which moderates confidence.

However, buildsTowards is not supported: the Term 4 bullet shows no expanded capability over the Term 3 bullet (no longer texts, more independence, or greater comprehension demand), it is a different performative response mode rather than a deepening, and the second endpoint's supplied Learning Component metadata records a second claim under the Grade R TERM 3 ancestor path (83d99627 / f5f4d44a / f48bd00a / ccbc8651), showing 'Acts out a story, song or rhyme' is already printed in Term 3 alongside the first endpoint. A skill co-occurring in the same term as the putative source cannot be a later developmental step from it; this is CAPS recurrence rather than progression. Canonical relatesTo (null direction, endpoint order unchanged) therefore records the meaningful reinforcement without asserting dependency or sequence. Material limitations: both endpoints omit 24 source-evidence items and all endpoint and ancestor SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context, so this rests on the printed bullet text, identity scope and supplied LCs; absence from the bounded excerpt is not proof of absence in the full source.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade R (coordinate rank 0) Skill bullets within the Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skill Area. The second SFI sits under Term 3, sub-strand 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning' ('Looks carefully at pictures and talks about common experiences', LCs 'Looks carefully at pictures' and 'Talks about common experiences'); the first sits under Term 4, sub-strand 'Uses language to investigate and explore' ('Asks questions and looks to books, television, computers for explanations', LCs 'Asks questions' and 'Looks to books, television, computers for explanations'). They share non-generic instructional coherence: each pairs purposeful attention to an external information source with oral expression, so teaching one meaningfully reinforces the other within the same Grade R oral-language strand in adjacent terms. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency in either direction: these are two distinct printed sub-strands addressing different capabilities (interpreting visual/pictorial cues versus enquiry and information-seeking from media), and the nomination signals are weak and largely lexical (shared tokens 'and'/'looks' with jaccard 0.12, LC tag overlap 'oral'/'speaking' with jaccard 0.13, a shared Grade R ancestor, and weak zero-gap rank proximity). Nothing indicates that proficiency in careful picture observation and talk about common experiences expands into, or materially supports success in, framing questions and consulting books, television and computers for explanations. relatesTo is therefore the correct symmetric judgment with null direction and unchanged canonical endpoint order. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and the first endpoint's supporting LC evidence is truncated, and because all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context: the Grade R and Term 3/Term 4 banners are merged repeated header occurrences, and each Skill bullet is a singleton separated from a shared table row.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 Reading and Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' (Phonics) Skills. The second SFI (Grade 2, Term 1) revises recognition of common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th) in word-final position with worked examples; the first SFI (Grade 2, Term 3) requires actively building words using the consonant and vowel digraphs, consonant blends and double consonants taught across the year. This is substantive expansion within one grade: from revising a small set of known consonant digraphs in one position to generative word building across a broader set of digraphs, blends and double consonants. Secure recognition of the Term 1 digraphs supports success in the Term 3 word-building skill, and the direction runs from the earlier Term 1 statement to the later Term 3 statement, which is permitted within the grade. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, but the full statement texts, identity scopes (grade/term/skill area/sub-strand) and Learning Component tags are present and consistent.

Shared ancestors and the only overlapping tokens ('and', 'emergent', 'reading') are not by themselves relational evidence. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skills under the same-named sub-strand 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities', the first in Term 1 ('Expresses feelings about a text and gives reasons'; LCs 'Expresses feelings about a text', 'Gives reasons for feelings expressed about a text') and the second in Term 4 ('Listens for the detail in stories and answers open-ended questions'; LCs 'Listens for the detail in stories', 'Answers open-ended questions'). These are distinct printed bullets addressing complementary oral-response capabilities: volunteering a justified personal reaction to a text versus attending to story detail and responding to a teacher-posed open-ended opinion question. There is genuine instructional coherence in Grade 3 focussed oral work on responding to texts, and the Term 4 exemplar ('Do you think it is right...?') meaningfully reinforces the Term 1 opinion-and-reason work. However, the evidence shows no substantive expansion of the same capability (no greater length, range, or independence of the Term 1 skill) and no justified dependency: answering open-ended questions and listening for detail do not, on this evidence, require prior proficiency in expressing feelings with reasons. Nomination signals are weak and non-semantic (shared Grade ancestor, zero rank gap, and overlap limited to generic tokens 'the', 'to', 'that', 'have', 'e', 'g' plus the single tag 'speaking'), so symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards is warranted. Limitations: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), the second endpoint's LC metadata is truncated, and the Grade and Term ancestor nodes are merged banner headers, so term placement rests on per-SFI identity_scope_values.

Second SFI: Grade 2 / Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading — 'Answers higher order questions based on the text read, e.g., "In your opinion…"' (LC tags: comprehension, higher order questions, opinion, reading). Both coordinates resolve to Grade 2 (rank 2), so a Term 1 -> Term 4 buildsTowards would be structurally allowed, but the pair-specific evidence does not show a substantively extended capability: these are two distinct, concurrently taught sub-strand practices (levelled group reading performance versus scaffolded whole-class inferential/evaluative response), and Shared Reading deliberately supports text access so that comprehension work is not conditioned on the learner's own instructional reading level. The shared Grade ancestor, rank_gap 0, stopword-dominated token/trigram overlap ('based', 'in', 'on', 'the') and the single generic shared LC tag 'reading' are not dependency evidence. The connection is nevertheless more than generic repetition: both are Grade 2 Reading and Phonics text-engagement skills within one reading programme, where levelled reading and higher-order response to read texts are complementary and mutually reinforcing, giving useful instructional coherence without sequence or dependency. Canonical relatesTo with null direction. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints sit in Grade R (coordinate rank 0), but the second SFI is under Term 1 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) ('Listens to and recalls simple word sequences, in order ... so that memory of what the ears have heard is developed'), while the first is under Term 3 / Emergent Reading, Emergent reading skills ('Recalls details and states main idea from a story read by the teacher'). Within the same grade, the permitted developmental direction is earlier Term 1 to later Term 3, i.e. second_to_first. The Term 1 statement explicitly targets auditory memory and ordered recall of what has been heard (LC tags 'auditory memory', 'listening', 'recall'), which plausibly supports the Term 3 demand of holding and reporting details and the main idea of a teacher-read story (LCs 'Recalls details from a story read by the teacher' and 'States the main idea of a story read by the teacher'). The change is substantive, not mere repeated wording: from short word sequences to connected narrative content with comprehension (main idea). Evidence limitation: lexical overlap between the two statements is low (shared tokens 'recalls', 'listening'), the shift from phonological/auditory-memory practice to narrative comprehension is an inferred support rather than a stated prerequisite, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3, Term 4 Skills in the same CAPS grade/term window but in different skill areas: the first is a Handwriting bullet under WRITING ('Uses the joined script or cursive writing for all written recording'), the second a Paired/Independent Reading bullet under READING AND PHONICS ('Reads own and others' writing'). They cohere substantively because legible joined handwriting is what makes learners' own and peers' written texts readable, and reading peer writing reinforces the purpose of neat recording; this is complementary production/reception coherence, not a dependency. No source evidence shows either as a staged precursor of the other, and they sit in the same Term so no grade/term ordering supports a developmental direction; the only lexical link is the generic token 'writing' (jaccard ~0.07), which is too weak for buildsTowards. Endpoint source evidence and the second SFI's LC metadata are truncated, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts shown.
